papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack file pdf/P-114.txt is the San-Martin et al. EEG/LORETA paper (BSPC 66 (2021) 102499), P-112's paper. The paper the record means (claim '93% Acc', registry row Kinect/ANFIS gait, summaries.md header 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195) is Seifallahi et al., 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system', BSPC 71 (2022) 103195, present in the pack as pdf/P-115.txt. Both read in full; verdict uses the gait paper.

Segmental disturbance of white matter microstructure in predicting mild cognitive impairment in idiopathic Parkinson's disease: An individualized study based on automated fiber quantification tractography (Yu et al., Parkinsonism and Related Disorders 115 (2023) 105802)

what_each_reports.P-114: Kinect V2 dual-task gait features, 150 older adults (70 MCI, 80 HC, Tehran), hierarchical ANFIS accuracy 93% (sens 90%, F-score 91.5%); evaluation protocol for ANFIS not stated.
what_each_reports.P-91: DTI automated fiber quantification in idiopathic Parkinson's disease: 30 IPD-MCI, 40 IPD with normal cognition, 30 HC. SVM (RBF) on pointwise FA/MD plus clinical features, trained on 70% of the IPD group with 10-fold CV and tested on a 30% stratified hold-out, discriminating IPD-MCI from IPD-NCI: validation AUC 0.80, balanced accuracy 0.79, sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.75 (training AUC 0.82, BA 0.85).

quantity_a: Accuracy of ANFIS on gait features, MCI vs cognitively healthy older adults (general memory-association population), protocol unstated
quantity_b: Hold-out ROC-AUC of an SVM on DTI tract-profile features, Parkinson's disease with MCI vs Parkinson's disease with normal cognition
incompatible_if_same: No. 93% accuracy and an AUC of 0.80 are different metric types; accuracy at one threshold cannot contradict an area under the ROC curve, and neither study claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch in substance: both are coded T1, but P-91's contrast is PD-MCI vs PD with normal cognition (a within-Parkinson's comparison), not MCI vs healthy controls
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: own IDAA Tehran cohort vs own First Hospital of China Medical University cohort; no waiver
gates.validation_tier: mismatch/uncertain: P-91 internal 70/30 stratified hold-out; P-114 protocol unstated
gates.modality_family: mismatch: gait/motor vs diffusion MRI (DTI tractography); no waiver

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: accuracy vs ROC-AUC; different population (idiopathic Parkinson's disease) and different comparison class (PD-NCI rather than healthy controls)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither row flagged; no contested value reaches 0.97.
independence: Independent: different groups, countries, cohorts; no shared authors.
grounds: The population behind the shared 'MCI' label differs: P-91 studies MCI in idiopathic Parkinson's disease under MDS Task Force criteria, P-114 studies MCI in general older adults.
The comparison differs: P-91 separates PD-MCI from PD patients with normal cognition, P-114 separates MCI from healthy controls.
The metric type differs: P-91's 0.80 is a ROC-AUC, P-114's 93% is accuracy.
The modality-family gate (gait vs DTI) and dataset-family gate (separate own cohorts) both fail with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
Forty IPD with normal cognition (IPD-NCI), thirty IPD-MCI, and thirty healthy controls were included.
The SVM model with defined hyperparameters (C = 3.175, Gamma = 0.007) showed preferable performance in differentiating IPD-NCI with IPD-MCI based on pointwise analysis results
validation dataset: balanced accuracy = 0.79; AUC = 0.80; sensitivity = 0.78; specificity = 0.75
The IPD group was separated into training (70%) and validation (30%) dataset with stratified random sampling.

record_defects: The pack's P-114 PDF (paper_pdf_map.json, 'formula-unverified') is P-112's EEG paper, not the gait/ANFIS paper the record means.
claim_b 'P-91: AUC 0.80 on T1' omits that the contrast is PD-MCI vs PD-NCI in Parkinson's disease, not MCI vs healthy controls.
dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong; validation_comparable='Yes' is unsupported.

The resolution note's 14 bridging papers (P-360, P-322, P-416, P-422, P-478, P-333, P-501, P-9, P-538, P-557, P-703, P-795, P-855, P-931) list scores from unrelated modalities and contrasts; none identifies a condition separating these two results, so partially_resolved_candidate is not supported. The P-795 entry is truncated prose.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers; they measure different contrasts in different populations with different metrics.
